examples.scenario: A decoded elevation prints as 0.1 but its stored binary float is not the exact decimal one tenth
examples.reason: Displayed decimal text is insufficient to reproduce the exact stored value.

examples.scenario: Positive zero and negative zero compare equal numerically but arise from different signed computations
examples.reason: The sign can expose a transformation or subtraction path difference even when the scalar value is zero.

examples.scenario: NumPy allclose accepts 1e-9 and 2e-9 with default tolerances
examples.reason: The documented default absolute tolerance is unsuitable for values much smaller than one.

examples.scenario: Two arrays contain NaN in the same cells and equal_nan=True returns equality
examples.reason: Matching invalid positions do not establish valid numeric elevation or height difference.

examples.scenario: Float32 values are summed along different axes and produce slightly different totals
examples.reason: NumPy summation precision can depend on axis and memory layout.

examples.scenario: An integer accumulator wraps during a support or uncertainty sum without raising an exception
examples.reason: NumPy documents modular integer arithmetic for sum, so overflow can look plausible.

examples.scenario: NumPy rounds 56294995342131.5 to three decimals as 56294995342131.51
examples.reason: The fast decimal-scaling algorithm can introduce a visible last-digit error.

examples.scenario: Decimal is constructed implicitly from a float and later quantized with no inspection of Inexact or Rounded
examples.reason: Exact float conversion preserves the binary artifact and silent quantization can discard digits.
